title: Compatibility and independence of common-stage cones
statement:
If $M\subset N$, exactness of $T_{N/M}$ identifies the scalar extension of a
cone triangle for $u$ with a cone triangle for $u_N$. If two representatives
define the same morphism of $\mathcal P_T$, their cone triangles become
isomorphic after passage to a field where the representatives agree. Any two
cone triangles selected for one finite-stage morphism are isomorphic by a
morphism of triangles whose first two components are identities. Thus
distinguishedness in [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] is independent of
every representative, common field, and cone choice.

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this independence: the
blueprint adds the proof that distinguishedness of a common-stage triangle
is independent of the representative, the common field and the chosen cone,
which is what makes the pair category a triangulated category below. The
fixed-category input is Stacks': Lemma 13.4.7 ([Tag
014B](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/014B), fetched and quoted) states
that a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of a pre-triangulated category has a
distinguished triangle $(X,Y,Z,f,g,h)$ unique up to (nonunique) isomorphism
of triangles, more precisely that a second such triangle is related to the
first by an isomorphism $(1,1,c)$ — exactly the assertion that two cone
triangles are isomorphic by a morphism of triangles with identity on source
and target — with Lemma 13.4.3 ([Tag
014A](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/014A), if two of the three
components of a morphism of distinguished triangles are isomorphisms so is
the third). Difference: 014B is internal to one pre-triangulated category,
whereas the blueprint must also compare the cone triangles of the scalar
extensions $T_{N/M}$ and of different representatives of one morphism of
$\mathcal P_T$.

proof.text:
Fix the scheme, coefficient fields, rational categories $\mathcal C_E(T)$ and coherent extension functors of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. The finite-stage pre-triangulated structures are part of the exact-functor assertion of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], where exact has the meaning of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $u:X_M\to Y_M$ represent $f:(E,K)\to(F,L)$, with $X_M=T_{M/E}K$, $Y_M=T_{M/F}L$, and choose the distinguished triangle $X_M\xrightarrow{u}Y_M\xrightarrow{i}Z\xrightarrow{p}X_M[1]$ of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. For $M\subseteq N$ put $H=T_{N/M}$, $A_X=a_{N,M,E,K}$ and $A_Y=a_{N,M,F,L}$. Exactness of $H$ [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], in the meaning of [def-weil-triangulated-category], says that
$$HX_M\xrightarrow{H(u)}HY_M\xrightarrow{H(i)}HZ\xrightarrow{\sigma_{N/M,X_M}\circ H(p)}(HX_M)[1]$$
is distinguished. Replace its first and second objects using $A_X,A_Y$. The resulting triangle has arrows
$$u_N=A_Y\circ H(u)\circ A_X^{-1},\quad i_N=H(i)\circ A_Y^{-1},\quad p_N=A_X[1]\circ\sigma_{N/M,X_M}\circ H(p).$$
The triple $(A_X,A_Y,1_{HZ})$ is a triangle isomorphism: substitution verifies each of its three squares. TR1 therefore makes this a distinguished cone triangle of exactly the transported representative $u_N$. In Lean, exactness of the actual coefficient transition is obtained from the derived scalar adjunction: restriction is exact, so Mathlib triangulated-adjunction exactness makes its left adjoint exact. The fully faithful integral inclusion reflects exactness. The integral-image characterization of the published rational distinguished triangles, together with the shift-compatible integral/rational comparison, transfers this exactness to the actual rational scalar functor, including equal fields. These are the concrete finite-stage constructions of the already cited nodes.

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence: scalar extension and endpoint identifications

proof.text: For two distinguished triangles of the same finite-stage arrow $w:X\to Y$, the first square with $a=1_X,b=1_Y$ commutes, since both composites are $w$. TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] gives $c:Z\to Z'$ satisfying $c i=i'$ and $p'c=p$, hence a morphism of triangles $(1_X,1_Y,c)$. Both identity components are invertible; [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] therefore makes $c$ invertible. By the componentwise criterion of [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift], this is an isomorphism of triangles with the required identity first two components. This proves finite-stage cone-choice independence without asserting a unique or functorial choice of $c$.

source.place: Tag 014B, lemma-cone-triangle-unique-isomorphism, proof using TR3 and Tag 014A, lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle

proof.text: Suppose $(M,u)$ and $(N,v)$ represent the same morphism with the same pair-category endpoints. By [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] there is a finite overfield $Q\supseteq M,N$ such that $u_Q=v_Q$ as maps $T_{Q/E}K\to T_{Q/F}L$. Apply Step 1 to both chosen cone triangles; both resulting triangles in $\mathcal C_Q(T)$ are distinguished, and their first arrows agree literally, not merely as classes. Step 2 supplies an isomorphism between them with identity on these two common endpoints. If a further field is used, transport transitivity $(u_Q)_{Q'}=u_{Q'}$ and the finite-diagram equality criterion of [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] preserve the equality, so Step 1 again gives two distinguished triangles with the identical first arrow $u_{Q'}=v_{Q'}$, and Step 2 gives an isomorphism with identity first two components at $Q'$. Thus different representatives and different common overfields are compared at a finite stage where they agree.

source.place: ## Proof, second sentence: equivalent representatives over a common field

proof.text:
We verify that the scalar-extended triangle in Step 1 gives the same triangle in $\mathcal P_T$, up to an isomorphism with identity on $(E,K)$ and $(F,L)$. Its old cone is $(M,Z)$ and its new cone is $(N,HZ)$. Define $\eta:(M,Z)\to(N,HZ)$ and its inverse by the representatives $[N,1_{HZ}]$ in the two directions. These are typed because $T_{N/M}Z=HZ$ and $T_{N/N}=1$. The composition formula of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] gives identities at stage $N$, which represent the pair identities by the unit equations and representative-independence of [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]. The second-arrow square is precisely $i_N=H(i)A_Y^{-1}$. For the third arrow, the coherence of shift comparisons with associators in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] reads
$$A_X[1]\circ\sigma_{N/M,X_M}\circ H(\sigma_{M/E,K})=\sigma_{N/E,K}\circ a_{N,M,E,K[1]}.$$
Consequently transport of the old third-arrow representative is
$$a_{N,M,E,K[1]}\circ H(\sigma_{M/E,K}^{-1}\circ p)=\sigma_{N/E,K}^{-1}\circ A_X[1]\circ\sigma_{N/M,X_M}\circ H(p)=\sigma_{N/E,K}^{-1}\circ p_N.$$
This is exactly the new third arrow prescribed by [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. The first-arrow square is equality of the two representatives of $f$. The definition of triangle morphisms and its componentwise isomorphism criterion [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift] now give the claimed pair-category triangle isomorphism. The Lean implementation uses commonStageConeIso, Functor.mapTriangleIso, Functor.mapTriangleCompIso, and transportedConeIso to form this comparison. Compatibility of transIso with shifts follows directly from the recorded associator shift coherence. The endpoint equations reduce to the stage-system cocycle; no pretriangulation on the pair category is assumed.

source.place: ## Proof, transport via common-stage calculus and sigma comparisons, all three squares expanded

proof.text:
For the two triangles compared over $Q$ in Step 3, put $W=T_{Q/M}Z$ and $W'=T_{Q/N}Z'$ and write their third-component isomorphism as $c:W\to W'$. The corresponding common-stage cone triangles at $Q$ have cone objects $(Q,W)$ and $(Q,W')$. Their comparison has third component $[Q,c]:(Q,W)\to(Q,W')$, with inverse $[Q,c^{-1}]$; these composites are the pair identities $[Q,1_W]$ and $[Q,1_{W'}]$ by [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. The first two components are the pair identities, so their first square is equality of the classes of $u_Q=v_Q$. The second square is $c i_Q=i'_Q$. The last square is
$$\sigma_{Q/E,K}^{-1}p'_Q c=\sigma_{Q/E,K}^{-1}p_Q,$$
obtained by composing $p'_Q c=p_Q$ with $\sigma_{Q/E,K}^{-1}$; these are exactly the third arrows of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. The pair identity on $(E,K)$ shifts to the identity on $(E,K[1])$ by [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]. Thus [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift] gives an isomorphism $\gamma$ between the two cone triangles at $Q$. Write $\alpha$ and $\beta$ for the Step 4 isomorphisms from the original triangles to their respective extensions at $Q$. Then $\beta^{-1}\gamma\alpha$ is a typed triangle isomorphism between the original choices, with identity first two components. Its cone component is $[Q,c]:(M,Z)\to(N,Z')$, since the cone components of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are represented at $Q$ by identities. Taking $M=N=Q$ covers two cone choices for a single representative.

source.place: ## Proof, comparison over the agreement field and passage to pair-category triangles

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones], distinguishedness means that a triangle is isomorphic to a common-stage cone triangle. Steps 4 and 5 show that replacing any representative, common field or cone changes this witness only by a triangle isomorphism. Compose the witnessing isomorphism with the comparison to obtain a witness using the replacement, and use the inverse comparison for the converse. Composition and inverses are those of the triangle category [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift]. This proves independence of distinguishedness in its defined, existential sense.

proof.text:
For $M\subset N$, the functor $T_{N/M}$ of
[prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] is exact and its shift comparison carries
the cone triangle for $u$ in $\mathcal C_M$ to a distinguished triangle of
$\mathcal C_N$ which is a cone triangle for $u_N$, identifying the scalar
extension of the first with a cone triangle of the second. If
$(M,u)\sim(N,v)$, then $u_P=v_P$ for some finite $P$, and transporting the
two cone triangles to $P$ via the transport of
[prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] and the $\sigma$-comparisons of
[prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] makes them isomorphic over $P$ by the
finite-stage axiom TR3, with identity components on the common source and
target; any two cone triangles selected for one finite-stage morphism are
isomorphic by a morphism of triangles whose first two components are
identities (the finite-stage uniqueness of cones up to noncanonical
isomorphism). Combining these facts, distinguishedness in
[def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] is independent of the representative, of
the common field and of the cone choice, in the sense of the category of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category].
